A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLMBias study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material. Reporting inconsistencies in some new results do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original VLM evaluations, linear-probing experiments, prompting and tool-use analyses, and a 78-participant human study, including quantitative results in Tables 2–20.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds intermediate-layer probes, rectangle-counting controls, prompting experiments, paired-image comparisons and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The core VLMBias construction procedure remains subject selection, counterfactual image generation or editing, and human quality control (Section 3; Appendices E–K). The added diagnostic experiments do not introduce a revised benchmark-construction algorithm, model architecture or training objective.

E1.justification: The seven original domains remain intact. v3 adds an abstract four-versus-five-rectangle dataset in A.8 and a paired-image task asking whether original and counterfactual animals have equal leg counts in A.22. These extend coverage with focused control scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds locate-then-count prompting as an evaluated alternative to Q1/Q2 (Table 23), and compares neutral with subject-name prompts (Tables 24–25). The evaluated VLM roster remains unchanged; the expanded Table 12 largely consolidates model comparisons already reported separately in v2.

E3.justification: The main evaluation settings are retained, while new diagnostic protocols add probes after projection and at the last LLM layer, a rectangle control with matched splits, performance conditional on tool or pointing activation, prompt manipulations, paired-image judgments and attention extraction. Section 3.2 also changes the named logo-generation model from o4-mini to Gemini-2.0 Flash, although Appendix F remains unchanged; this does not establish regenerated data.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands investigations of failure mechanisms: representation-stage and rectangle controls (A.8), conditional tool and pointing analyses (A.15–A.16), localization prompts, subject-name prompts and direct visual comparison (A.20–A.22), and attention heatmaps (A.23). New qualitative examples examine failed procedural counting and successful versus incorrect cropping (M.2 and M.5).

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same five-run study of o4-mini and Sonnet-3.7, including identical mean-plus/minus values, pass@5, agreement and self-reported confidence statistics in Table 10. v3 introduces no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: The principal benchmark scores remain unchanged. New results include animal probe accuracies of 91.24% after projection and 89.08% at the last LLM layer (Table 8), 51.59% accuracy on tool-activated cases (Table 15), and 11.76% correct paired-image judgments (Table 26). These concern added conditions, not same-setting performance improvements. Elephant predictions for Moondream-2B and Molmo-72B also change from 4 to 5 in v2 Figures 32/34 versus v3 Figures 38/40.

T1.justification: The bias-rate definition, image-scaling formula and patterned-grid construction mathematics are retained. The added probes and attention analyses are empirical investigations; no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions and claims: severe counterfactual visual bias across seven domains, improved accuracy after background removal, and declining accuracy with excessive reasoning. The additional appendix evidence supports these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: In A.15, v3 replaces v2's explanation that generic visual tools may be less suitable than specialized pointing with an explanation emphasizing effective tools but insufficient activation. It also interprets intermediate probes and attention maps as evidence that available visual information is overridden during answer generation. New cropping examples identify incorrect localization as a tool-use failure condition.

D1.justification: v3 documents 896-dimensional pooled features for the added probes, attention extraction from answer tokens, explicit prompts for new experiments, and the rectangle dataset's matched split. It also specifies that the existing animal crop covers the lower half containing the legs. Model-access tables and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a counting-focused discussion citing work such as Paiss et al., Campbell et al., Xu et al. and Yin et al., positioning VLMBias against ordinary counting evaluations. A.23 adds links to attention–answer disconnect research by Liu et al. and Zhang et al. The existing bias/hallucination positioning and Appendix C benchmark comparisons are retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and heading revisions, expands the counting discussion and rewrites A.8. It adds a detailed contents list and groups previously separate prompt and qualitative appendices under L and M. The main narrative sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 8 and consolidates existing model results in Table 12, while adding tables for conditional activation, prompting and paired-image tests. New figures present probe trajectories, attention heatmaps, paired inputs and qualitative failures or successes. Figure 6 receives revised axis labeling, and existing supplementary displays are relocated into the reorganized appendices.

improvement.justification: The rectangle controls, intermediate probes and additional prompting/comparison tests make v2's bias interpretation more informative and assessable. However, comparisons involving self-selected tool/pointing subsets do not establish causal gains, and new reporting inconsistencies limit the benefit: rectangle accuracy is 65.52% in Table 8 but 66.52% in A.8, while Molmo-72B's bias reduction is 0.91 points in Table 19 but 8.09 in A.16. The added diagnostic value supports a limited net improvement; decisive causal attribution remains unresolved.
